messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate observed in rate-limiter service: 502/503s upstream while contacting managed cache (MemScale) - automatic page fired.
sofia: I’m on it, grabbing pager. Any customer impact yet?
ben: seeing client 429 spikes in us-west for token-issuance route. latency up ~200ms+ and repeated upstream connect failures.
chaim: logs show `TLS handshake failed: remote_error` when connecting to MemScale auth gateway. happened around 12:07 UTC.
samira: confirmed on telemetry: MemScale control plane returned 5xx during auth refresh which causes our connection pooling to go into backoff.
sofia: ok triage plan — 1) open incident, 2) add mitigation, 3) escalate to vendor if not recovered in 15m. I’ll start playbook.
sofia: creating incident channel #inc-1799302468 and posting initial status.
ben: adding brief to customers-dashboard: some requests may see rate-limit enforcement because cache auth failures cause fallback to strict token checks.
chaim: quick mitigation: flip rate-limiter to degraded-local-cache mode (serve rules from local snapshot) to avoid upstream auth calls. Running rollout now.
samira: +1 do that, but note local snapshot TTL is 30s — might still cause short bursts. we'll extend TTL to 5m for now.
sofia: running command: ```curl -X POST https://control-plane/internal/feature-flags -d '{"service.rate_limiter.degraded_local_cache": true}'```
sofia: set snapshot_ttl to 300s.
support-bot: action logged: feature flag toggled by sofia. audit-id: ae3b-179930.
ben: router metrics stabilizing, 429s dropping but some 5xx remnant from other flows. Seems like cache-dependent endpoints are recovering slower.
chaim: pushing additional change: bump per-connection backoff windows to avoid thundering retries: set CONNECT_BACKOFF=10s -> 30s for MemScale.
samira: also disabling prefix caching for auth-keys to avoid returning stale denies while handshake is flaky.
sofia: reaching out to MemScale support: "we're seeing TLS handshake errors from multiple regions since 12:07 UTC — can you confirm control-plane status?"
sofia: MemScale responded: "Investigating certificate rotation edge-case causing handshake failures for some clients."
ben: vendor claims certificate rollover but only affects certain ciphers — our client libs use a fallback cipher suite? need immediate workaround.
chaim: workaround proposed: force our connections to prefer RSA cipher suite and disable the problematic ECDHE fallback. Pushing config change to client TLS stack now.
samira: rolling change to TLS prefs in downstream pool config: ```tls_preference: [RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384]```
sofia: note to on-call: this is the handoff window, I need to step out in 20m. @oncall-rotation please pick up if not resolved.
oncall-rotation: acknowledged, I’ll follow the runbook and coordinate with MemScale.
ben: while TLS flip is rolling, I want to call out that some customers on Dedicated who use strict rate limits might have seen token denials — we should prepare a customer message.
sofia: drafting status update: "We’re observing degraded traffic for auth-dependent endpoints due to a third-party cache provider certificate rotation issue. We have enabled degraded local rate-limiter mode and rolled TLS preference changes; mitigation in progress. No data loss."
samira: logs show TLS-preference rollout reduced handshake failures by ~85% in eu-west. us-west lagging due to old connection pools.
chaim: forcing pool restarts for us-west workers now: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/rate-limiter -n prod --selector=region=us-west`
ben: pool restart done; metrics look green. 5xxs near baseline and 429s back to normal.
sofia: excellent. set incident status -> RED -> GREEN? I’ll move to MONITORING and prepare postmortem template.
support-bot: incident status changed to MONITORING by sofia.
sofia: we still need vendor RCA and long-term fix: ensure MemScale certificate rotations share new root and supported ciphers in advance. Opening vendor ticket and adding to P0 follow-up.
oncall-rotation: taking over. I will keep the incident open until vendor confirms root-cause. tagging follow-ups: on-call to create PR to add longer local snapshot TTL and safer TLS preferences with tests.
ben: adding note: ensure our rate-limiter has a non-blocking fallthrough when auth provider is degraded (so we don't cascade 5xxs).
chaim: agreed; created issue INF-4927 for non-blocking fallthrough and improved pool health checks.
samira: kudos to team — mitigation worked quickly. Recommend we expand simulated cert rotation tests in e2e harness.
sofia: closing handoff — thanks all. I’ll update the incident timeline and notify SRE rotation. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident channel archived; follow-up tasks created: INF-4927, vendor-ticket-2246.
sofia: brief postmortem to be posted in /postmortems within 72h.
end of thread
